results.title: Kripke model of a CSLib model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on a nonempty type of worlds, the associated Kripke model has the same worlds, the binary accessibility relation of $m$ as its accessibility relation, and the valuation of $m$ as its valuation.

results.title: The translation preserves satisfaction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m$ be a CSLib unimodal model on a nonempty type of worlds, $w$ a world and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Then the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis holds at $w$ in the Kripke model of $m$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $m$.

results.title: The CSLib unimodal model of a Kripke model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A Kripke model $k$ on worlds $W$ gives the CSLib unimodal model on $W$ whose frame is the unimodal frame built from the accessibility relation of $k$ and whose valuation is the valuation of $k$.

results.title: Kripke to CSLib and back is the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a Kripke model on a nonempty type of worlds. Converting $k$ to a CSLib unimodal model and converting that model back to a Kripke model gives $k$.

results.title: Round trip from CSLib models through Kripke models
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a nonempty type of worlds $W$, converting a CSLib unimodal model $m$ on $W$ into a Kripke model and then back into a CSLib unimodal model returns $m$: a unimodal frame is determined by its binary accessibility relation.

results.title: The reverse translation preserves satisfaction
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $k$ be a Kripke model, $w$ a world and $\varphi$ a modal formula in the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis. Then $\varphi$ holds at $w$ in $k$ if and only if its translation into a CSLib unimodal proposition holds at $w$ in the CSLib model associated with $k$.

results.title: Validity agrees with its CSLib translation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is valid in a Kripke model $k$ (true at every world of $k$) if and only if its translation into a CSLib unimodal proposition is satisfied at every world of the CSLib unimodal model associated with $k$.

results.title: Validity of the translation gives membership in CSLib's logic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $S$ be a class of CSLib unimodal models on a type of worlds and $\varphi$ a CSLib unimodal proposition. Suppose that, if the type of worlds is nonempty, the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is valid in the Kripke model of every model in $S$. Then $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's semantic logic of $S$: it holds at every world of every model in $S$.

results.title: Soundness for CSLib's K
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system K, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic K: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type.

results.title: Soundness for CSLib's T
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. If the translation of $\varphi$ into the $\bot$, $\to$, $\Box$ basis is a theorem of the Hilbert system T, then, for every type of worlds, $\varphi$ belongs to CSLib's modal logic T: it holds at every world of every CSLib unimodal model on that type whose accessibility relation is reflexive.

results.title: Soundness for CSLib's S4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. results.title: Soundness for CSLib's S5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\varphi$ be a CSLib unimodal proposition. results.title: Consistency relative to a normal modal logic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sets of formulas $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$, the set $\Gamma$ is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ when $\bot$ is not deducible from $\Gamma$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.

results.title: Consistency is of finite character
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, a set of formulas is consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ iff all its finite subsets are.

results.title: Lindenbaum's lemma for normal modal logics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas that is consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$ is contained in a set $M$ of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to $\mathrm{K} \oplus \Lambda$.

results.title: Maximal consistent sets of modal formulas are deductively closed
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$. Every formula that is a local consequence of $M$ in that logic belongs to $M$.

results.title: Iterated modus ponens in maximal consistent sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas, $M$ a set of modal formulas that is maximal among the sets consistent relative to the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, and $\varphi$ and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ modal formulas. If $\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots) \in M$ and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n \in M$, then $\varphi \in M$.

results.title: Discharging a list of hypotheses
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas, $\varphi$ a modal formula and $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ a list of modal formulas. If $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma \cup \{\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n\}$ in the normal modal logic K extended by the axioms $\Lambda$, then $\gamma_1 \to (\gamma_2 \to \cdots \to (\gamma_n \to \varphi) \cdots)$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in the same logic.

results.title: Boxing an implication chain
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of extra axioms, let $\gamma_1, \dots, \gamma_n$ be formulas (with $n \ge 0$) and let $\varphi$ be a formula. Then $\Box(\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \gamma_n \to \varphi) \to (\Box\gamma_1 \to \cdots \to \Box\gamma_n \to \Box\varphi)$ is a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$.

results.title: Worlds of the canonical model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of extra axioms, the worlds of the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$: the sets of formulas that are consistent relative to $K \oplus \Lambda$ and have no consistent proper superset.

results.title: The canonical accessibility relation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $\Lambda$ of modal formulas and maximal $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent sets $M$ and $N$ (worlds of the canonical model), $M$ is related to $N$ iff every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$ belongs to $N$.

The canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ is the Kripke model whose worlds are the maximal consistent sets of $K \oplus \Lambda$ (there is at least one, by Lindenbaum's lemma), in which $M$ sees $N$ iff $\varphi \in N$ for every formula $\varphi$ with $\Box\varphi \in M$, and in which an atom $p$ is true at $M$ iff…

results.title: Truth lemma
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A formula holds at a world of the canonical model iff it belongs to it.

results.title: Deducibility from maximal consistent extensions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ and $\Gamma$ be sets of modal formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ belongs to every maximal $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set that contains $\Gamma$, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.

results.title: Completeness relative to the canonical model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas such that $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$, let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. If $\varphi$ holds at every world of the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds, then $\Gamma$ deduces $\varphi$ in $K \oplus \Lambda$.

results.title: Local semantic consequence over a class of Kripke models
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $C$ be a class of Kripke models, given as a predicate on models. A set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas locally entails a formula $\varphi$ over $C$ when, for every Kripke model $M$ in $C$ whose type of worlds lies in the universe of the atoms and every world $w$ of $M$, if every formula of $\Gamma$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$, then $\varphi$ is satisfied at $w$ in $M$.

results.title: Strong completeness of K
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in K.

results.title: Strong completeness of T
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in T.

results.title: Strong completeness of S4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in S4.

results.title: Strong completeness of S5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a set of formulas and $\varphi$ a formula. Suppose that for every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and whose worlds form a type in the universe of the atoms, and every world $w$ of it at which all formulas of $\Gamma$ hold, $\varphi$ holds at $w$. Then $\varphi$ is deducible from $\Gamma$ in S5.

results.title: Soundness and completeness of K
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of K if and only if $\varphi$ is valid, that is, true at every world, in every Kripke model whose worlds live in the universe of the atoms.

results.title: Soundness and completeness of T
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of T if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.

results.title: Soundness and completeness of S4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S4 if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is reflexive and transitive and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.

results.title: Soundness and completeness of S5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A modal formula $\varphi$ is a theorem of S5 if and only if $\varphi$ is valid in every Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation and whose type of worlds lies in the same universe as the type of atoms.

results.title: Model existence from the canonical model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Lambda$ be a set of modal formulas and $C$ a class of Kripke models whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, such that $C$ contains the canonical model of $K \oplus \Lambda$ whenever $\bot$ is not a theorem of $K \oplus \Lambda$. Then every $(K \oplus \Lambda)$-consistent set $\Gamma$ of formulas is satisfiable in $C$: some model in $C$ has a world at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Model existence for K
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every K-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Model existence for T
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every T-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a reflexive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Model existence for S4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every S4-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a reflexive transitive Kripke model, whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Model existence for S5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every S5-consistent set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas there are a Kripke model whose accessibility relation is an equivalence and whose worlds lie in the universe of the atoms, and a world of it at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Strong soundness and completeness of K
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in K if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over all Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Strong soundness and completeness of T
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in T if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model with reflexive accessibility relation, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S4 if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over reflexive transitive Kripke models: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every Kripke model with reflexive and transitive accessibility relation, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Strong soundness and completeness of S5
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $\Gamma$ of modal formulas and every modal formula $\varphi$, $\varphi$ is a local consequence of $\Gamma$ in S5 if and only if $\Gamma$ locally entails $\varphi$ over Kripke models whose accessibility relation is an equivalence relation: $\varphi$ holds at every world of every such Kripke model, with worlds in the universe of the atoms, at which every formula of $\Gamma$ holds.

results.title: Isomorphism-closed classes of groups (Kourovka 12.91)
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A class of groups is a property of groups (in the lowest type universe) that is closed under isomorphism: whenever a group $H$ has the property and $H$ is isomorphic to a group $K$, then $K$ has the property. Only the finite members of a class are used in Kourovka Problem 12.91.

results.title: Fitting classes (Kourovka 12.91)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups is a Fitting class (of finite groups) if, for every finite group $G$: whenever $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, every normal subgroup of $G$ belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$; and whenever $N_1$ and $N_2$ are normal subgroups of $G$ that belong to $\mathfrak{X}$, the subgroup $N_1 N_2$ they generate belongs to $\mathfrak{X}$.

results.title: Supersoluble groups (Kourovka 12.91)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble if it has a chain of subgroups $1 = G_0 \le G_1 \le \cdots \le G_k = G$, each normal in $G$, such that for every $i < k$ there is an element $x \in G_{i+1}$ with $G_{i+1} = \langle x \rangle G_i$; that is, every factor $G_{i+1}/G_i$ is cyclic.

results.title: Minimal normal subgroups (Kourovka 12.91)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $N$ of a group $G$ is minimal normal if $N$ is a nontrivial normal subgroup of $G$ and every nontrivial normal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $M \le N$ equals $N$.

results.title: Heineken's question on Fitting classes of supersoluble groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups that is a Fitting class and all of whose finite members are supersoluble, every minimal normal subgroup of every finite group $G \in \mathfrak{X}$ is contained in the center of $G$.

results.title: A Fitting class of supersoluble groups with a non-central minimal normal subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a class $\mathfrak{X}$ of groups that is a Fitting class and all of whose finite members are supersoluble, a finite group $G \in \mathfrak{X}$, and a minimal normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ that is not contained in the center of $G$.

results.title: Base of a group action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$ acting on a set $\Omega$, a finite set $B \subseteq \Omega$ is a base when its pointwise stabilizer is trivial: the only $g \in G$ with $g \cdot \omega = \omega$ for all $\omega \in B$ is $g = 1$.

results.title: Minimal base
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$ acting on a set $\Omega$, a finite set $B \subseteq \Omega$ is a minimal base when it is a base, that is, its pointwise stabilizer in $G$ is trivial, and for every $\omega \in B$ the set $B \setminus \{\omega\}$ is not a base.

results.title: Maximal size of a minimal base
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, the number $b(G)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the sizes of the minimal bases of $G$ over all actions of $G$ on a set $\Omega$, where a minimal base is a finite set $B \subseteq \Omega$ whose pointwise stabilizer in $G$ is trivial while that of $B \setminus \{\omega\}$ is not, for every $\omega \in B$. It is the largest such size when these sizes are bounded, as they are for finite $G$, and…

results.title: Independent subset of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite subset $S$ of a group $G$ is independent when no element $s \in S$ lies in the subgroup of $G$ generated by $S \setminus \{s\}$.

results.title: Maximal size of an independent set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, a finite subset $S \subseteq G$ is independent when no $s \in S$ lies in the subgroup generated by $S \setminus \{s\}$. The number $\mu'(G)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{N}$ of the sizes of the finite independent subsets of $G$: their largest size when these sizes are bounded, as they are for finite $G$, and $0$ when they are unbounded.

results.title: Cameron's question on minimal bases and independent sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that $b(G) = \mu'(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $b(G)$ is the largest size of a minimal base of $G$ over all actions of $G$ on a set, and $\mu'(G)$ is the largest size of an independent subset of $G$ (a subset none of whose elements lies in the subgroup generated by the others).

results.title: Kourovka Problem 16.45 has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not true that $b(G) = \mu'(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $b(G)$ is the largest size of a minimal base of $G$ over all actions of $G$ on a set, and $\mu'(G)$ is the largest size of an independent subset of $G$.

results.title: The closed square
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The closed square $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, the product of two copies of the unit interval, used as a model of the closed disc.

results.title: Boundary of the square
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The boundary $\partial I^2$ of the closed square $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ is the set of points $(x, y) \in I^2$ with $x = 0$, $x = 1$, $y = 0$ or $y = 1$.

results.title: Boundary-fixing homeomorphisms of the square
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ be the closed square and $\partial I^2$ its boundary. $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ is the subgroup of the group of homeomorphisms of $I^2$ consisting of those homeomorphisms $h$ with $h(x) = x$ for every $x \in \partial I^2$.

results.title: Right orders of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The right orders of `G`: linear orders (as relations) invariant under right multiplication.

results.title: Right-orderability of the boundary-fixing homeomorphisms of the disc
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition (Kourovka Problem 17.20, G. M. Bergman, for the closed disc) that the group $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ of homeomorphisms of the closed square $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$, a model of the closed disc, that fix the boundary $\partial I^2$ pointwise is right-orderable: it carries a linear order $\le$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c$.

results.title: Boundary-fixing homeomorphisms of the disc are not right-orderable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $I^2 = [0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ be the closed square, a model of the closed disc, and let $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ be the group of homeomorphisms of $I^2$ that fix every point of the boundary $\partial I^2$. There is no linear order $\le$ on $\mathrm{Homeo}(I^2; \partial I^2)$ such that $a \le b$ implies $ac \le bc$ for all $a, b, c$; that is, this group is not right-orderable.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then the real part of the determinant of $A$ is at most the product of the real parts of its diagonal entries: $\operatorname{Re} \det A \le \prod_{i=1}^{n} \operatorname{Re} A_{ii}$.

results.title: AM–GM inequality for the determinant of a positive semidefinite matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then $(\operatorname{Re} \det A)^{1/n} \le \operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{tr} A)/n$.

results.title: AM–GM inequality for the determinant of a positive semidefinite matrix, power form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then $\operatorname{Re} \det A \le (\operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{tr} A)/n)^n$.

results.title: Equality in the AM–GM bound for the determinant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrix. Then $(\operatorname{Re} \det A)^{1/n} = \operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{tr} A)/n$ if and only if $A = cI$ for some real number $c \ge 0$, where $I$ is the $n \times n$ identity matrix.

results.title: The trace of a product of positive semidefinite matrices has nonnegative real part
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be positive semidefinite complex $n \times n$ matrices. Then the real part of the trace of $AB$ is nonnegative: $\operatorname{Re} \operatorname{tr}(AB) \ge 0$.

results.title: Squares of natural numbers modulo 8
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $r$, the remainder of $r^2$ on division by $8$ is $0$, $1$ or $4$.

results.title: Numbers congruent to 3 mod 8 are not squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a natural number $n$ satisfies $n \equiv 3 \pmod 8$, then $n$ is not the square of a natural number.

results.title: Numbers congruent to 6 mod 8 are not squares
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a natural number $n$ satisfies $n \equiv 6 \pmod 8$, then $n$ is not the square of a natural number.

results.title: A number that is 6 mod 8 minus a smaller square is not a square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $N \equiv 6 \pmod 8$ and $k^2 < N$. Then $N - k^2$ is not the square of a natural number.

results.title: Odd squares modulo 16
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every odd natural number $k$, either $k^2 \equiv 1 \pmod{16}$ and $k \equiv 1$ or $7 \pmod 8$, or $k^2 \equiv 9 \pmod{16}$ and $k \equiv 3$ or $5 \pmod 8$.

results.title: Squares of integers modulo 8
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $x$, the remainder of $x^2$ on division by $8$, taken in $\{0, 1, \dots, 7\}$, is $0$, $1$ or $4$.

results.title: Dilatation of a p-adic polynomial at a point
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, $f \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ and $x_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_p$. Dilatation data for $f$ at $x_0$ consist of a natural number $e$ and a polynomial $g \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ such that $g(X) = p^{-e} f(x_0 + pX)$ as polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}_p$, and the reduction of $g$ modulo $p$ is nonzero.

results.title: Dilatation of the constant polynomial one at zero
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every prime $p$, the exponent $e = 0$ and the polynomial $g = 1$ form dilatation data for the constant polynomial $1 \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ at the point $x_0 = 0$.

results.title: Existence of dilatations of p-adic polynomials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $f \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ have nonzero reduction modulo $p$. Then for every $x_0 \in \mathbb{Z}_p$ there are a natural number $e$ and a polynomial $g \in \mathbb{Z}_p[X]$ with nonzero reduction modulo $p$ such that $g(X) = p^{-e} f(x_0 + pX)$ as polynomials over $\mathbb{Q}_p$; that is, dilatation data for $f$ at $x_0$ exist.

results.title: The $p$-adic valuation of an integer polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be a nonzero polynomial, with $a_n$ the coefficient of $X^n$ in $f$. Writing $v_p(a)$ for the $p$-adic valuation of an integer $a$, the $p$-adic valuation of $f$ is the natural number $v_p(f) = \min \{ v_p(a_n) : a_n \neq 0 \}$.

results.title: The valuation of a polynomial is at most that of each nonzero coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, write $v_p(a)$ for the $p$-adic valuation of an integer $a$, let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be a nonzero polynomial with $a_n$ the coefficient of $X^n$ in $f$, and let $v_p(f) = \min \{ v_p(a_n) : a_n \neq 0 \}$ be its $p$-adic valuation. If $a_n \neq 0$, then $v_p(f) \le v_p(a_n)$.

results.title: Lower bounds for the valuation of a polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, write $v_p(a)$ for the $p$-adic valuation of an integer $a$, let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be a nonzero polynomial with $a_n$ the coefficient of $X^n$ in $f$, and let $v_p(f) = \min \{ v_p(a_n) : a_n \neq 0 \}$ be its $p$-adic valuation. If $k$ is a natural number with $k \le v_p(a_n)$ for every $n$ with $a_n \neq 0$, then $k \le v_p(f)$.

results.title: The valuation of a nonzero constant polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $a$ be a nonzero integer. The $p$-adic valuation of the constant polynomial $a \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$, the minimum of the $p$-adic valuations of its nonzero coefficients, equals the $p$-adic valuation $v_p(a)$ of the integer $a$.

results.title: Negated remainder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $k \ge 1$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $k$ is the unique $u$ with $0 \le u < k$ and $u \equiv -n \pmod{k}$: it equals $0$ when $k$ divides $n$ and $k - (n \bmod k)$ otherwise. For $k = 0$ it is defined to be $0$.

results.title: Characterization of the negated remainder
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $u$ with $k \ne 0$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $k$ equals $u$ if and only if $u < k$ and $k$ divides $n + u$.

results.title: Engel remainder trajectory
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is the sequence $t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ of natural numbers with $t_0 = a$ and, for every $j \ge 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$, while if $t_j \ne 0$ then $t_{j+1}$ is the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$: the unique natural number $u < t_j$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t_j}$. Once the trajectory reaches $0$ it stays there.

results.title: Initial term of the Engel trajectory
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ has value $a$ at step $0$.

results.title: Zero is absorbing for the Engel trajectory
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then $t_{j+1} = 0$.

results.title: Step of the Engel trajectory at a nonzero term
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j \ne 0$, then $t_{j+1}$ is the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$: the unique natural number $u < t_j$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t_j}$.

results.title: First step of the Engel trajectory
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $t \ne 0$. Then the Engel remainder trajectory of $t$ with respect to $n$ is, at step $1$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t$: the unique natural number $u < t$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t}$.

results.title: An Engel trajectory started at $a$ vanishes within $a + 1$ steps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers and let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. Then $t_i = 0$ for some $i \le a + 1$.

reading_title.source: An Engel trajectory started at $a$ vanishes within $a + 1$ steps

results.title: Engel trajectories vanish at a positive step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers and let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. Then $t_j = 0$ for some $j \ge 1$.

results.title: Engel length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. The Engel length $L(n, a)$ is the least $j \ge 1$ with $t_j = 0$.

results.title: The Engel length is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ satisfies $L(n, a) \ge 1$.

results.title: Engel trajectory vanishes at the Engel length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $L$ be the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$. Then the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is $0$ at step $L$.

results.title: The Engel length is at most any positive vanishing step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$, and let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then the Engel length $L(n, a)$ satisfies $L(n, a) \le j$.

results.title: Engel trajectory is nonzero at positive steps before the Engel length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $L$ be the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $1 \le j < L$, then the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is nonzero at step $j$.

results.title: Maximal Engel length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the maximal Engel length is $M(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} L(n, a)$, where $L(n, a)$ is the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$; for $n = 0$ the maximum is over the empty set and $M(0) = 0$.

results.title: Each Engel length is at most the maximal Engel length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a \le n$. Then the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ is at most the maximal Engel length $M(n) = \max_{1 \le b \le n} L(n, b)$.

results.title: A uniform bound on Engel lengths bounds the maximal Engel length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $B$ be natural numbers. If the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ satisfies $L(n, a) \le B$ for every $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, then the maximal Engel length $M(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} L(n, a)$ (with $M(0) = 0$) satisfies $M(n) \le B$.

results.title: Fresh variables reserved for a clause
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of fresh variables reserved for a CNF clause $C$ in the SAT-to-3SAT translation: $k - 1$ if $C$ has $k \ge 1$ literals, and $0$ if $C$ is empty.

results.title: Clause-by-clause translation with a fresh-number counter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula this returns a pair $(N, \psi)$ of a natural number $N$ and a CNF formula $\psi$. The empty formula gives $N = 0$ and $\psi$ empty. A formula with first clause $C$ and remaining clauses $\varphi'$, whose pair is $(N', \psi')$, gives $N = N' + \max(|C| - 1, 0)$ and, as $\psi$, the chain of clauses replacing $C$ with fresh numbers from $N'$ on, followed by the clauses of $\psi'$.

results.title: The SAT-to-3SAT translation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a CNF formula with clauses $C_1, \dots, C_m$, the translation is the concatenation, in order, of the chains of clauses replacing $C_1, \dots, C_m$, where the chain for $C_i$ uses fresh numbers from $u_i = \sum_{j > i} \max(|C_j| - 1, 0)$ on.

results.title: The SAT-to-3SAT reduction on bit strings
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A bit string that decodes, with no bits left over, to a CNF formula $\varphi$ is sent to the binary code of the SAT-to-3SAT translation of $\varphi$; any other bit string is sent to the empty string.

results.title: Chain-tail clauses have at most three literals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every clause $C$ and natural number $z$, every clause of $\mathrm{chainTail}(C, z)$ has at most three literals.

results.title: Chain clauses have at most three literals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every clause $C$ and natural number $u$, every clause of $\mathrm{chain}(C, u)$ has at most three literals.

results.title: Clauses of the auxiliary 3SAT translation have at most three literals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, every clause of the clause list produced by the auxiliary SAT-to-3SAT translation of $\varphi$ (which replaces each clause by its chain of clauses with fresh variables) has at most three literals.

results.title: The SAT-to-3SAT translation yields clauses of length at most three
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, every clause of the translation $\mathrm{to3}(\varphi)$ has at most three literals.

results.title: Soundness of the tail of a chain

results.title: Soundness of the chain of one clause
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $C$ be a clause and $u$ a natural number. If an assignment $v'$ satisfies every clause of $\mathrm{chain}(C, u)$, then the assignment $n \mapsto v'(2n)$ satisfies $C$.

results.title: Soundness of the auxiliary 3SAT translation

results.title: Lifting an assignment to the 3SAT translation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ and a CNF formula $\varphi$, the lifted assignment sends an even variable $n$ to $v(n/2)$ and an odd variable $n$ to the fresh-variable value built from $v$ and $\varphi$ at the number $\lfloor \log_2 (n - 1) \rfloor - 1$, where $\lfloor \log_2 0 \rfloor$ is taken to be $0$ and subtraction is truncated at $0$.

results.title: The lifted assignment on renamed variables
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every assignment $v : \mathbb{N} \to \mathrm{Bool}$, every CNF formula $\varphi$ and every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the assignment lifted from $v$ for the 3SAT translation of $\varphi$ gives the renamed variable $2n$ the value $v(n)$.

results.title: The SAT-to-3SAT translation preserves satisfiability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the translation $\mathrm{to3}(\varphi)$ is satisfiable if and only if $\varphi$ is satisfiable.

results.title: CNF encodings are nonempty
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the binary encoding of $\varphi$ is not the empty bit string.

results.title: Correctness of the SAT-to-3SAT reduction on bit strings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit string $x$, SAT accepts $x$ (that is, $x$ encodes a satisfiable CNF formula) exactly when 3SAT accepts the image of $x$ under the SAT-to-3SAT reduction (that is, the image encodes a satisfiable CNF formula in which every clause has at most three literals).

results.title: Binary representation of a fresh name
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $z$, the binary representation (least significant bit first) of $\mathrm{fresh}(z) = 2^{z+1} + 1$ is $\mathrm{true}$, then $z$ copies of $\mathrm{false}$, then $\mathrm{true}$.

results.title: Code of a fresh literal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $z$ and every polarity $b$, the binary code of the literal $(\mathrm{fresh}(z), b)$, where $\mathrm{fresh}(z) = 2^{z+1} + 1$, is $\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{true}$, then $z$ copies of the pair $\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}$, then $\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}, b$.

results.title: Code of a renamed literal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every literal $(n, p)$, the binary code of the renamed literal $(2n, p)$ is: the pair $\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}$ if $n \neq 0$ and nothing if $n = 0$, then the pair $\mathrm{true}, b$ for each bit $b$ of the binary representation of $n$ (least significant bit first, no bits for $n = 0$), then $\mathrm{false}, p$.

results.title: Stacks of the 3SAT emitter
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The 3SAT emitter machine has six stacks: the token stack $T$, the output stack $O$, the fresh counter $U$, two scratch counters $Z$ and $W$, and the output clause count $C$.

results.title: Stack alphabets of the SAT-to-3SAT emitter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The output stack of the emitter machine holds Booleans; each of its other stacks (the token stack, the fresh counter, the two scratch counters and the output clause count) holds symbols of the SAT verifier's token alphabet.

results.title: Control labels of the SAT-to-3SAT emitter
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The emitter machine has the labels $\mathrm{start}$, $\mathrm{clause}$, $\mathrm{fin}$ and $\mathrm{done}$, and, for Booleans $f, p, s, x, e$, the labels $\mathrm{lit}(f)$, $\mathrm{fa}(s, x)$, $\mathrm{fb}(s, x)$, $\mathrm{fc}(s, x)$, $\mathrm{fd}(s, x)$, $\mathrm{fe}(s, x)$, $\mathrm{body}(f, p)$, $\mathrm{cp}(f, e)$, $\mathrm{aft}(f)$ and $\mathrm{sfx}(f)$, all distinct; equality of labels is decidable.

results.title: Literal-marker test of the 3SAT emitter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an optional token $s$ (the top of a stack, absent when the stack is empty), the test is true exactly when $s$ is present and is a literal marker, of either polarity.

results.title: Entry label of a literal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For Booleans $f$ and $p$, the label where the emitter continues after popping the marker of a literal of polarity $p$ is $\mathrm{body}(\text{true}, p)$, which copies the name directly, if $f$ holds (the literal is the first walked in its clause), and $\mathrm{fa}(\text{true}, p)$, which first prepends the fresh literal of the current counter with polarity true, otherwise.

results.title: Return label of the fresh-literal subroutine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For Booleans $s$ and $x$, the label where the emitter continues after prepending the fresh literal of polarity $s$ is $\mathrm{body}(\text{false}, x)$ if $s$ is true, which copies the name of the pending literal of polarity $x$, and $\mathrm{sfx}(x)$ if $s$ is false, which closes the output clause, $x$ being the first-literal flag.

results.title: The SAT-to-3SAT emitter machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The emitter is the multi-stack machine on the stacks $T, O, U, Z, W, C$ of the emitter ($O$ holds bits, the others token symbols), with the labels of the emitter and one internal Boolean variable. results.title: Start label of the SAT-to-3SAT emitter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The start label of the emitter machine is its label $\mathrm{start}$, at which the machine begins each input clause or, once the token stack is empty, moves on to its final phase, which writes the output clause count.

results.title: Stack contents of the SAT-to-3SAT emitter

results.title: Stacks of the tokenize-then-emit machine
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The stacks of the tokenize-then-emit machine for an emitter $E$ are the disjoint union of the SAT tokenizer's stacks and $E$'s stacks.

results.title: Alphabets of the tokenize-then-emit machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an emitter $E$, every stack of the combined machine that comes from the SAT tokenizer has the tokenizer's symbol alphabet, and every stack $k$ that comes from $E$ has the alphabet of $k$ in $E$.

results.title: Labels of the tokenize-then-emit machine
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For an emitter $E$, the labels of the combined machine form the disjoint union of the SAT tokenizer's labels, the labels of $E$, and the two booleans: false labels the step that writes the output $E$ fixes for undecodable input, and true is the exit label.

results.title: Exit label of the tokenize-then-emit machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The labels of the tokenize-then-emit machine for an emitter $E$ are the SAT tokenizer's labels, $E$'s labels and two extra labels indexed by the booleans; the exit label is the extra label indexed by true.

results.title: Tokenizer stacks in the tokenize-then-emit machine
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Embedding the tokenizer's stacks into tokenize-then-emit
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Embedding the emitter's stacks into tokenize-then-emit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The stack embedding of an emitter $E$ into the tokenize-then-emit machine for $E$: each stack of $E$ goes to its own copy among the emitter stacks of the combined machine, which carries the same alphabet, and symbols are left unchanged.

results.title: Renaming the tokenizer's labels

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: The SAT-to-3SAT reduction is polynomial-time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The map on bit strings that sends the binary encoding of a CNF formula $\varphi$ to the binary encoding of the SAT-to-3SAT translation of $\varphi$, and sends every bit string that encodes no CNF formula to the empty bit string, is computable in polynomial time.

results.title: SAT reduces to 3SAT
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem SAT, which accepts exactly the bit strings that encode a satisfiable CNF formula, has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to the decision problem 3SAT, which accepts exactly the bit strings that encode a satisfiable CNF formula with at most three literals per clause.

results.title: 3SAT is NP-hard
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to the decision problem 3SAT, which accepts exactly the bit strings that encode a satisfiable CNF formula with at most three literals per clause.

results.title: 3SAT is NP-complete
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The decision problem 3SAT, which accepts exactly the bit strings that encode a satisfiable CNF formula with at most three literals per clause, is in NP, and every decision problem in NP has a polynomial-time many-one reduction to 3SAT.

results.title: Window product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to M$ in a monoid $M$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$, the window product is the ordered product $x_a x_{a+1} \cdots x_{b-1}$ of the terms with indices $a \le j < b$; it is the empty product $1$ when $b \le a$.

results.title: Prefix product
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $x_0, x_1, \dots$ in a monoid $M$ and a natural number $i$, the prefix product at $i$ is $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$, the factors taken in increasing order of index.

results.title: Products of adjacent windows
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid and $x : \mathbb{N} \to M$ a sequence, and for $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$ let $x_{[a, b)}$ be the ordered product $x_a x_{a+1} \cdots x_{b-1}$ (equal to $1$ if $b \le a$). For all $a \le b \le c$, $x_{[a, b)} \, x_{[b, c)} = x_{[a, c)}$.

results.title: The Kogge–Stone scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a sequence $x_0, x_1, \dots$ in a monoid $M$, the value $s_k(i)$ at position $i$ after $k$ rounds is defined by $s_0(i) = x_i$ and, for each $k$, $s_{k+1}(i) = s_k(i - 2^k) \, s_k(i)$ if $2^k \le i$ and $s_{k+1}(i) = s_k(i)$ otherwise.

results.title: What the scan holds after each round
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_0, x_1, \dots$ be a sequence in a monoid $M$, let $k$ and $i$ be natural numbers, and let $m = \min(i + 1, 2^k)$. After $k$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan, position $i$ holds the product $x_{i+1-m} \cdots x_i$ of the $m$ consecutive inputs ending at $i$, taken in increasing order of index.

results.title: The scan computes all prefix products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_0, x_1, \dots$ be a sequence in a monoid $M$ and let $n$ and $K$ be natural numbers with $n \le 2^K$. After $K$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan, every position $i < n$ holds the prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$.

results.title: Work of a scan round
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The work of round $k$ on $n$ positions is $\max(n - 2^k, 0)$, the number of positions $i < n$ with $i \ge 2^k$, each of which performs one multiplication.

results.title: The work of a round counts its combining positions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the work of round $k$ on $n$ positions equals the number of positions $i$ with $2^k \le i < n$.

results.title: Work of the Kogge–Stone scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total work of $K$ rounds on $n$ positions is $\sum_{k=0}^{K-1} \max(n - 2^k, 0)$, the sum over the rounds $k < K$ of the work $\max(n - 2^k, 0)$ of round $k$.

results.title: Work bound for the Kogge–Stone scan
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all $n, K \in \mathbb{N}$, the total work of $K$ rounds of the scan on $n$ positions is at most $nK$.

results.title: Span of the Kogge–Stone scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The span of $K$ rounds of the scan is $K$: each round is one parallel step.

results.title: The scan computes all prefixes in logarithmically many rounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_0, x_1, \dots$ be a sequence in a monoid $M$ and let $n$ be a natural number. After $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan (the least $K$ with $n \le 2^K$), every position $i < n$ holds the prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$.

results.title: One round of the scan on a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list $y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}$ in a monoid $M$ and a natural number $k$, one round produces the list of length $n$ whose entry $i$ is $y_{i - 2^k} \, y_i$ when $2^k \le i$ and $y_i$ when $i < 2^k$.

results.title: Tabulated Kogge–Stone scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{n-1})$ in a monoid $M$, the list after $K$ rounds is defined by recursion on $K$: after $0$ rounds it is $y$, and after $K + 1$ rounds it is round $K$ applied to the list after $K$ rounds. Here round $k$ sends a list $(z_0, \dots, z_{n-1})$ to the list of length $n$ whose entry $i$ is $z_i$ for $i < 2^k$ and $z_{i - 2^k} z_i$ for $2^k \le i < n$.

results.title: The tabulated scan agrees with the round recursion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ be a list of elements of a monoid $M$, extended to a sequence by $x_j = 1$ for $j \ge n$. For every number of rounds $K$ and every position $i < n$, entry $i$ of the list produced by $K$ rounds of the tabulated scan equals the value at position $i$ after $K$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan applied to the sequence $x$.

results.title: The tabulated scan computes all prefix products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ be a list of elements of a monoid $M$ and let $K$ be a natural number with $n \le 2^K$. Then for every $i < n$, entry $i$ of the list produced by $K$ rounds of the tabulated scan equals the prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$.

results.title: Adjacent pair products of a sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $x \colon \mathbb{N} \to M$ in a monoid $M$, the sequence of adjacent pair products is the sequence whose term at $i$ is $x(2i) \cdot x(2i+1)$.

results.title: Blelloch's scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid. For a natural number $k$ and a sequence $x = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ in $M$, the scan $B_k(x)$ is the sequence in $M$ defined by recursion on $k$: $B_0(x)$ is constantly $1$, and $B_{k+1}(x)$ is obtained from the scan $y = B_k(p)$ of the pair products $p_i = x_{2i} x_{2i+1}$ by setting $B_{k+1}(x)_{2i} = y_i$ and $B_{k+1}(x)_{2i+1} = y_i x_{2i}$ for every $i$.

results.title: Blelloch's scan computes the exclusive prefix products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid, $k$ a natural number and $x = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $M$. For every $j < 2^k$, the value at position $j$ of Blelloch's scan of $x$ on $2^k$ positions is the exclusive prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{j-1}$ (equal to $1$ when $j = 0$).

results.title: Work of Blelloch's scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number $W(k)$ of monoid multiplications Blelloch's scan performs on $2^k$ positions is defined by $W(0) = 0$ and $W(k+1) = 2^k + W(k) + 2^k$: on $2^{k+1}$ positions, $2^k$ pair products, the recursive scan on the $2^k$ pair products, and $2^k$ products for the odd positions.

results.title: Parallel steps of Blelloch's scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The span $S(k)$ of Blelloch's scan on $2^k$ positions is defined by $S(0) = 0$ and $S(k+1) = S(k) + 2$: one parallel step for the pair products, the recursive scan, and one parallel step for the odd positions.

results.title: Blelloch's scan is work-efficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $W(k)$ of monoid multiplications Blelloch's scan performs on $n = 2^k$ positions satisfies $W(k) + 2 = 2^{k+1}$, so $W(k) = 2^{k+1} - 2 < 2n$.

results.title: Blelloch's scan has logarithmic span
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $k$, the span of Blelloch's scan on $n = 2^k$ positions is $2k = 2 \log_2 n$.

results.title: Adjacent pair products of a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list $[a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1}]$ of elements of a monoid $M$, the list of adjacent pair products is $[a_0 a_1, a_2 a_3, \ldots]$: it has length $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, its $i$-th entry is $a_{2i} a_{2i+1}$, and when $n$ is odd the last element $a_{n-1}$ is dropped.

results.title: Interleaving step of Blelloch's list scan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid. For lists $z = (z_0, z_1, \dots)$ and $x = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ in $M$, the expansion of $z$ along $x$ is the list $(z_0, z_0 x_0, z_1, z_1 x_2, z_2, z_2 x_4, \dots)$: each $z_i$ is followed by $z_i x_{2i}$, and the list stops at the first $i$ for which $z_i$ or $x_{2i+1}$ does not exist.

results.title: Blelloch's scan on lists
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid. For a natural number $k$ and a list $xs = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ in $M$, the list scan $L_k(xs)$ is defined by recursion on $k$: $L_0(xs)$ is the one-element list $(1)$, and $L_{k+1}(xs)$ is obtained from the list scan $z = L_k(p)$ of the pair products $p = (x_0 x_1, x_2 x_3, \dots)$ of $xs$ (a trailing unpaired entry is dropped) by interleaving: $L_{k+1}(xs) = (z_0, z_0 x_0, z_1, z_1 x_2, \dots)$,…

results.title: The list implementation computes Blelloch's scan
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid, $k$ a natural number and $xs = (x_0, \dots, x_{2^k - 1})$ a list in $M$ of length $2^k$. For every $j < 2^k$, the entry at position $j$ of Blelloch's list scan of $xs$ in $k$ rounds equals the value at position $j$ of Blelloch's scan on $2^k$ positions of the sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{2^k - 1}, 1, 1, \dots$ obtained by extending $xs$ by $1$.

results.title: The list implementation computes the exclusive prefix products
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid, $k$ a natural number and $xs = (x_0, \dots, x_{2^k - 1})$ a list in $M$ of length $2^k$. For every $j < 2^k$, the entry at position $j$ of Blelloch's list scan of $xs$ in $k$ rounds is the exclusive prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{j-1}$ (equal to $1$ when $j = 0$).
